newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer but off highs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer but off highs.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen interest rate futures closed firmer on Monday, but off highs, as the topside was capped on growing concerns that the market was overbought.
The contract was also weighed down by the Nikkei stock index's close at a calendar year high, traders said.
Expectations that corporate sentiment in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey, due June 25, may have worsened provided recent upward momentum for the market, they said.
But they said the bulls became hesitant to buy further.
"It is impossible (for us) to buy further above 99.10 without bearish economic news, like a slowdown in Japan's economic recovery this summer," said a city bank dealer.

A long-term credit bank dealer echoed that view: "We understand the tankan is going to show a worsening in corporate sentiment due to the yen's recent rise against the dollar. But even so, we cannot buy further toward 99.20 as the BOJ will not cut its discount rate."
The December settled at 99.09, retaining its strength from Friday's night session, when it rose as high as 99.10.
After ending the day session at 99.05 on Friday, the contract fell briefly on larger-than-expected growth in Japan's gross domestic product for the January-to-March quarter.

But December soon rebounded later in the night session mainly on short-squeezing due to a growing view that no other economic data was likely to give the BOJ a reason to raise interest rates before next week's tankan survey.
Such a view also prompted city banks to receive fixed interest rates at the short- to medium-zone of the interest rate swap (IRS) market late on Friday, traders said.

On Monday, IRS rates recovered from late Friday's levels amid light trade. The three-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.48/1.52 percent as of 0732 GMT. On Friday, the three-year IRS rate fell as low as 1.485 percent after fears of higher interest rates subsided. Before Friday's release of the GDP data, the rate was traded at 1.53 percent.
The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.49 percent on Monday after the BOJ left the market with neither a surplus nor a shortall by draining 200 billion yen.
The neutral operation was what the market had expected on the first day of the new bank reserve reporting period.
On Friday, the key short-term interest rate fell to 0.43 percent due to low bank demand for funds on the last day of the bank reserve period.
Long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered only at 0.59 percent on Monday. The offer rate was unchanged from Friday's issued rate.
